links.outcome: HF rehospitalization and composite clinical events, AI-guided monitoring vs standard care
links.effect: HF rehospitalization 16.3% vs 18.7% (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.43-1.84; P=0.76); composite HR 1.03 (0.63-1.70); AI-detected instability reduced (HR 0.76)
links.quote: In exploratory analyses, HF rehospitalization occurred in 13 (16.3%) patients in the intervention group and 17 (18.7%) in the control group (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.43-1.84; P = 0.76).

links.outcome: Heart failure rehospitalization with AI-guided monitoring versus standard care

links.quote: In exploratory analyses, HF rehospitalization occurred in 13 (16.3%) patients in the intervention group and 17 (18.7%) in the control group (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.43-1.84; P = 0.76).

links.outcome: Notification response timeliness and implementation barriers under a structured clinician response algorithm
links.effect: Clinicians responded within a median of 1 day (range: 1-5 days); clinician engagement was high, but workflow integration and response uncertainty were primary implementation barriers.
links.quote: Median monitoring adherence was 72.4% of follow-up days; clinicians responded to communicated notifications within a median of 1 day (range: 1-5 days), and qualitative analysis demonstrated high patient acceptance and clinician engagement, whereas identifying workflow integration and response uncertainty as the primary barriers to implementation.
